question: Can I target my opponent's Soltari Priest with Lightning Bolt?
expected: No. Soltari Priest has protection from red, so it can't be targeted by red spells like Lightning Bolt.

question: If I cast Wrath of God while my opponent controls Darksteel Colossus, does the Colossus die?
expected: No. Darksteel Colossus is indestructible, so 'destroy' doesn't affect it; it stays on the battlefield.

question: My opponent casts Lightning Bolt on my Grizzly Bears and I respond with Giant Growth on the Bears. Do the Bears survive?
expected: Yes. Giant Growth resolves first, the Bears become 5/5, and 3 damage isn't lethal, so they survive until end of turn.

question: I just played Llanowar Elves this turn. Can I tap it for mana right away?
expected: No. It has summoning sickness: a creature can't use {T} abilities unless you've controlled it continuously since your most recent turn began.

question: My opponent counters my Mulldrifter with Counterspell. Do I still draw two cards?
expected: No. The countered spell never enters the battlefield, so its enters trigger never happens.

question: Can I cast Giant Growth on my own Gladecover Scout?
expected: Yes. Hexproof only stops spells and abilities your opponents control from targeting it; you can target your own hexproof creature.

question: Can I put Rancor on my own Argothian Enchantress?
expected: No. Shroud means it can't be the target of any spells or abilities, including yours, and an Aura spell targets.

question: My opponent casts Sudden Shock targeting my Grizzly Bears. Can I respond with Giant Growth to save them?
expected: No. Sudden Shock has split second, so while it's on the stack players can't cast spells (only mana abilities and special actions), so the Bears die.

question: I cast Abrupt Decay and my opponent responds with Counterspell targeting it. What happens?
expected: Counterspell can be cast and resolves, but it doesn't counter Abrupt Decay, which can't be countered; Abrupt Decay resolves normally.

question: I cast Raging Goblin this turn. Can it attack right away?
expected: Yes. Raging Goblin has haste, so it can attack the turn it comes under your control.

question: My opponent controls Leyline of Sanctity. Can I target them with Thoughtseize?
expected: No. While they control Leyline of Sanctity, that player has hexproof and can't be the target of spells or abilities you control.
source: Leyline of Sanctity Oracle text; CR 702.11c

question: I control Platinum Angel and my life total is -5. Do I lose the game?
expected: No. Platinum Angel says you can't lose the game, so the state-based action for having 0 or less life doesn't make you lose while you control it.

question: Can my opponent respond to me tapping Llanowar Elves for mana?
expected: No. It's a mana ability, which doesn't use the stack and resolves immediately, so it can't be responded to.

question: My opponent controls Thalia, Guardian of Thraben. How much do I have to pay to cast Lightning Bolt?
expected: {1}{R}. Thalia makes noncreature spells cost {1} more to cast.

question: Can my opponent block my Boggart Brute with just one creature?
expected: No. Boggart Brute has menace, so it can't be blocked except by two or more creatures.

question: With Blood Moon and Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth on the battlefield, are all lands Swamps?
expected: No. Blood Moon makes Urborg a Mountain that loses its ability, so Urborg doesn't make any lands Swamps, regardless of timestamp order.
source: Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth official ruling (Magus of the Moon / setting a basic land type)

question: My opponent has Leyline of the Void. If my Kitchen Finks dies, does persist bring it back?
expected: No. Kitchen Finks is exiled instead of going to the graveyard, so it doesn't die and persist doesn't trigger.
source: Leyline of the Void official ruling

question: If Torpor Orb is on the battlefield and I cast Mulldrifter normally, do I draw two cards?
expected: No. Torpor Orb stops creatures entering from causing triggered abilities to trigger, so Mulldrifter's draw doesn't happen.

question: I control Doubling Season and cast Jace Beleren. How much loyalty does Jace enter with?
expected: 6. Planeswalkers enter with double the normal loyalty counters under Doubling Season (Jace's starting loyalty is 3).

question: With Humility and Glorious Anthem on the battlefield, what size is my Grizzly Bears?
expected: 2/2. Humility sets base P/T to 1/1 (layer 7b) and Glorious Anthem's +1/+1 applies afterward (layer 7c).

question: My Colossal Dreadmaw is equipped with Basilisk Collar and is blocked by a 4/4. How much damage can I trample over to the player?
expected: 5. With deathtouch, 1 damage counts as lethal to the blocker, so you assign 1 to it and the remaining 5 of its 6 power to the player.

question: I cast Grasp of Darkness on my opponent's Darksteel Myr. Does it die?
expected: Yes. -4/-4 makes its toughness 0 or less, and the state-based action puts it into the graveyard; indestructible only stops destruction.

question: I control Doubling Season and cast Raise the Alarm. How many Soldier tokens do I get?
expected: Four. Doubling Season doubles the tokens created, so two become four.

question: I control Panharmonicon and cast Mulldrifter for its normal cost. How many cards do I draw?
expected: Four. Mulldrifter's enters trigger triggers an additional time, so it draws two cards twice.

question: Wrath of God destroys my Blood Artist and three other creatures at the same time. How many times does Blood Artist trigger?
expected: Four times: once for itself and once for each of the other three. Leaves-the-battlefield abilities look back in time, so Blood Artist sees all the creatures that died with it.

question: I control Phyrexian Unlife and I'm at 0 life. If a creature deals 3 damage to me, what happens?
expected: You get 3 poison counters instead of losing life (damage is dealt as though it had infect), and you don't lose for having 0 or less life.
source: Phyrexian Unlife Oracle text and rulings

question: My opponent's Chalice of the Void has one charge counter. What happens if I cast Lightning Bolt?
expected: Chalice triggers because Lightning Bolt's mana value equals the number of charge counters (1), and when the trigger resolves Lightning Bolt is countered.
source: Chalice of the Void Oracle text

question: My Clone copies my opponent's Grizzly Bears, which has two +1/+1 counters on it. How big is my Clone?
expected: 2/2. Counters aren't copiable values, so the Clone copies only the printed Grizzly Bears.

question: I control Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and cast Clone copying it. What happens?
expected: You control two legendary permanents with the same name, so the legend rule makes you choose one and put the other into your graveyard.

question: Can I use Stifle to counter the ability of my opponent's Polluted Delta?
expected: Yes. Stifle counters target activated or triggered ability, and Polluted Delta's ability is an activated ability that isn't a mana ability, so Stifle can counter it. Polluted Delta was already sacrificed as part of the cost, so your opponent doesn't search for a land.

question: I target my opponent's Sedgemoor Witch with Lightning Bolt and choose not to pay 3 life for ward. What happens?
expected: Ward triggers and, since you don't pay 3 life, Lightning Bolt is countered.

question: My opponent has Pithing Needle naming Jace Beleren. Can I still activate Jace's loyalty abilities?
expected: No. Loyalty abilities are activated abilities and they aren't mana abilities, so Pithing Needle stops them.

question: I cast my commander Atraxa, Praetors' Voice from the command zone for the third time this game. How much mana does it cost?
expected: Eight: its {G}{W}{U}{B} cost plus {4} commander tax, {2} for each previous time it was cast from the command zone.

question: I have Thassa's Oracle in my hand and my library is empty. What happens when I cast it?
expected: You win the game when its enters trigger resolves, because X (your devotion to blue) is always greater than or equal to the number of cards in your library (0).

question: Can I cast Stifle targeting the persist trigger of my opponent's Kitchen Finks?
expected: Yes. Persist is a triggered ability, so Stifle can counter it and Kitchen Finks stays in the graveyard.

question: Humility entered the battlefield before Opalescence. What are Humility's power, toughness and abilities now?
expected: Humility is a 4/4 enchantment creature with no abilities: Opalescence animates it (layer 4), Humility removes abilities (layer 6), and in layer 7b Humility's 1/1 applies first and Opalescence's 4/4 (later timestamp) overrides it.

question: If I have a Gandalf, Party Guest, a Sakashima of a Thousand Faces copying it and Samut, at the beginning of combat can I cast and resolve two spells with split second?
expected: Yes. Both triggers go on the stack; you cast a spell while the first resolves, that spell (split second) resolves, then the second trigger resolves and lets you cast the other.

question: My opponent's Phantasmal Image is copying a Grizzly Bears. If I cast Clone copying the Phantasmal Image, what does my Clone become?
expected: A Grizzly Bears that is also an Illusion and has 'When this creature becomes the target of a spell or ability, sacrifice it', because the copy exceptions become part of the copiable values.
source: CR 707.9b; Clone official ruling (copying a copy)

question: I control Laboratory Maniac with an empty library, but my opponent cast Angel's Grace this turn. If I draw a card, what happens?
expected: You don't win (Angel's Grace stops opponents winning this turn), but you don't lose either: the draw was still replaced by Laboratory Maniac.

question: My Kitchen Finks has a +1/+1 counter on it and my opponent puts three -1/-1 counters on it, so it dies. Does persist return it?
expected: No. When it dies it still has -1/-1 counters on it (the counters only cancel as a state-based action at the same time it dies), so persist doesn't return it.

question: I sacrifice my Grizzly Bears to Fling after casting Giant Growth on it this turn. How much damage does Fling deal?
expected: 5. Fling uses the sacrificed creature's power as it last existed on the battlefield, including Giant Growth's +3/+3.

question: I cascade with Bloodbraid Elf. Can I cast Fire // Ice from cascade?
expected: No. A split card's mana value in the library is the total of both halves (4), which isn't less than Bloodbraid Elf's mana value of 4, so cascade skips it.

question: What does Dryad Arbor look like while Blood Moon is on the battlefield?
expected: It is a land creature with land type Mountain (no longer Forest) and creature type Dryad, still a green 1/1, and it taps for {R}.

question: What happens to my Urza's Saga when my opponent's Blood Moon is on the battlefield?
expected: It isn't sacrificed. Blood Moon makes it a Mountain that loses its chapter abilities, and the state-based action that sacrifices a Saga applies only to a Saga with one or more chapter abilities.

question: I control Solemnity and Kitchen Finks. What happens when Kitchen Finks dies without counters on it?
expected: Persist returns Kitchen Finks, but Solemnity stops the -1/-1 counter from being put on it, so each time it dies again persist returns it again: a loop that repeats as long as something keeps killing it.

question: I control Melira, Sylvok Outcast, Kitchen Finks and Viscera Seer. How much life can I gain this turn?
expected: As much as you want. Sacrificing Kitchen Finks to Viscera Seer makes persist return it, Melira stops the -1/-1 counter so persist works again, and each return gains 2 life. It is an optional loop: you choose how many times to repeat it.
source: CR 702.79a, 732.2a; Melira and Kitchen Finks Oracle text

question: I control Exquisite Blood and Sanguine Bond and my opponent is at 10 life. What happens if my opponent loses 1 life?
expected: Your opponent loses the game. Each life loss triggers Exquisite Blood, and each life gain triggers Sanguine Bond, whose only legal target is your one opponent, so both triggers are mandatory and keep feeding each other. State-based actions are checked between them, so when your opponent reaches 0 life they lose. The loop is mandatory but it ends, so it is not a draw.

question: I cast Animate Dead on Worldgorger Dragon in my graveyard. It's the only creature card in any graveyard and no player has any other spells or abilities. What happens?
expected: The game is a draw. The Dragon's enter trigger exiles Animate Dead, so Animate Dead's leave trigger makes you sacrifice the Dragon. The Dragon's leave trigger then returns Animate Dead, which must enchant a creature card in a graveyard, and the Dragon is the only one, so it returns the Dragon again. Every step is mandatory and nothing can stop it, so the game is a draw.
source: CR 104.4b, 732.4; Worldgorger Dragon and Animate Dead Oracle text

question: My Youthful Knight attacks and is blocked by Grizzly Bears. What happens?
expected: Youthful Knight deals its 2 damage first, in the first-strike combat damage step, so Grizzly Bears dies before it can deal damage, and Youthful Knight survives.

question: ¿Puedo lanzar Giant Growth sobre mi propio Gladecover Scout?
expected: Sí. Hexproof solo impide que lo hagan objetivo los hechizos y habilidades de tus oponentes; puedes hacer objetivo a tu propia criatura con hexproof.

question: My Craw Wurm is blocked by Grizzly Bears and Llanowar Elves. Can I assign all 6 of its damage to Grizzly Bears?
expected: Yes. A creature blocked by two or more creatures divides its combat damage among them as its controller chooses, so all 6 can go to Grizzly Bears.

question: My opponent's commander Atraxa, Praetors' Voice has dealt me 18 combat damage this game. If it attacks me and deals 4 more combat damage, what happens?
expected: You lose the game: you've been dealt 21 or more combat damage by the same commander over the game, whatever your life total.

question: My commander Atraxa, Praetors' Voice is destroyed. Can I put it into the command zone?
expected: Yes. When your commander is put into a graveyard, you may put it into the command zone the next time state-based actions are checked.

question: My Grizzly Bears equipped with Embercleave attacks and is blocked by Llanowar Elves. How much damage does the defending player take?
expected: 5. The Bears are a 3/3 with double strike and trample: in the first-strike step they assign 1 lethal damage to the Elves and 2 to the player; the Elves die, and in the regular step all 3 damage tramples over to the player because no creature is blocking it.
